answer: An agent market requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, with the bond forfeited on cryptographic proof of signing conflicting commitments for the same order. Whether an agent sells lotus seeds, books a jetty berth, or grades an opal, the rule is identical. Running 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000, and each proven offense burns another bond; creating fresh names does not recover that money.
